inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average FY2025/26 (936,208k, FY2026 AR EPS note line 7842). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the share award scheme is funded by on-market purchases (US$4.0m FY26, US$7.0m FY25), so no new issuance.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income of US$30.8m (received US$29.7m) is classified in INVESTING activities, not OCF, so it is already outside reported FCF (OCF 471.1 - capex 287.0). Deducting it again would double-strip; the cash that earns it is added in the bridge instead.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR note 29(a)/EPS note: share-based payments US$8,437k (FY25 US$9,639k). No equity-award withholding taxes (shares bought on market for the award scheme).
inputs.fx_note: USD->HKD 7.8472, Yahoo HKD=X regularMarketPrice at 2026-10-10. HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band, which is the parity check (no USD dual listing). All flows modelled in USD and per-share values converted to HKD at this rate; refresh_price.py does not update it.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows (company reports and largely sells in USD). US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.15 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.0% cost of equity; net-cash balance sheet so WACC = CoE = 10.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality, China-JV share loss and tariff risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path 0.58% of revenue = FY26 lease principal US$18.0m + ~US$3m lease interest. Lease liabilities (US$59.2m) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~US$19m of the US$275m total) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (EBITDA includes NCI subsidiaries); NCI book stock US$42.8m deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI profit share is immaterial (+1.3m FY26, -2.3m FY25).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: non-US cyclical industrial / auto Tier-1 supplier -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). First valuation of this ticker. EBITDA margin anchored to ADJUSTED EBITDA (US$533.4m FY26 excl. US$22.4m intangible impairment and unrealized FX) plus SBC added back = 14.8% pre-SBC; FY25 was 16.0%, FY22-23 trough ~13-13.7%. FY2020 US$795.5m goodwill write-down excluded from all base judgments. Capex FY26 was elevated at 7.9% of sales (India/Chennai expansion) vs 4.9-5.4% FY24-25 and ~7.5% 10y average; path glides 7.8% -> 6.6%. Working capital capture -18% of the revenue change (receivables+inventory-payables = ~18% of sales; growth consumes cash). Interest paid on borrowings is not in the unlevered flows; debt is in the bridge. No open-market buyback programme: buyback_cash is award-scheme purchases only, so the flat count is a modelling convention barely funded by the company (SBC is only 0.23% of sales, so the gap is immaterial).

equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR balance sheet: 7.911 non-current + 4.623 current (US$000s); fair-value swings are excluded from the flows
FY26 AR note 16: obligations 27.245 less plan assets 0.498

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr, haircut (equity CAGR rejected: see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~5%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (0.0% 3yr / 3.0% 5yr) and 5yr EPS CAGR (-1.8%). Book growth is retained earnings on a flat-revenue business, not franchise growth, so revenue is the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income already outside OCF): FY21 155.6, FY23 199.1, FY26 175.7. Owner FCF CAGRs only modestly below reported because SBC is ~0.2-0.3% of sales. FY22 FCF was negative (-136m, working-capital build during the chip shortage) and FY20 net income carried the US$795.5m write-down; both are excluded as anchors.

base.narrative: Flat FY27 sales as APG keeps shedding Sino-foreign JV volume and US tariffs weigh, then 2-3% growth as domestic-China OEM, India and ITMS/thermal wins ramp; adjusted EBITDA margin recovers from 14.3% to a mid-cycle 15% as copper pass-through catches up; capex normalises from the India build.

bull.narrative: IPG growth accelerates on AI data-centre liquid-cooling pumps and the SOFC powder-metal line, humanoid-robot actuator JVs sign binding programmes, and domestic Chinese OEM wins more than replace JV losses; operating leverage returns margins to the FY18-19 16.5% level.

bear.narrative: Light-vehicle production slides, Sino-foreign JVs keep losing share faster than domestic-OEM wins ramp, broad US tariffs force price give-backs, and legacy IPG is commoditised by Chinese entrants; margin sits at the FY22-23 trough (~13-13.5%) and the new growth bets stay immaterial.

scenario_narratives.base: Auto volumes stay soft and the China JV customer mix keeps shrinking in FY27, but domestic-OEM, India and thermal-management wins plus IPG's liquid-cooling pumps restore ~2.5-3% growth; adjusted EBITDA margin back to a mid-cycle 15%, capex normalising after the India expansion. Net cash of ~US$0.58bn is a fifth of the market cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new-growth optionality the market priced in 2025 (AI liquid cooling, humanoid-robot actuators, SOFC components) starts to show in sales, and APG's re-positioning toward domestic Chinese OEMs works; growth runs 5-6% mid-decade and margins return to the FY18-19 peak of ~16.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The China JV share loss and US tariff regime compound a light-vehicle downturn: two years of falling sales, margins stuck at the FY22-23 trough, copper costs not fully recovered, and the robotics/cooling bets remain rounding errors.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: 84% auto exposure in a soft cycle, an ongoing structural customer-mix loss in China and unresolved US tariffs. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several nascent, unproven businesses (no binding robotics agreements disclosed) to scale at once. Base 50%. The net-cash balance sheet removes solvency risk, so the bear is an earnings case, not a distress case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF valuation of a net-cash global auto/industrial motor supplier. The 2025 AI/robotics re-rating has fully unwound; the question now is whether a business earning ~US$175m owner FCF with ~US$0.58bn net cash is worth more than its ~US$2.0bn market cap on ordinary auto-supplier economics, with the new businesses treated as bull-case optionality only.
key_risks_to_valuation: Light-vehicle production cycle and APG's 84% revenue weight
Pace of Sino-foreign JV share loss in China versus domestic-OEM wins
US tariff regime and in-region-for-region relocation costs
Copper and input-cost pass-through lag compressing margins
Capex staying at the FY26 7.9% level rather than normalising
Impairment / M&A integration risk (US$22.4m European intangible impairment FY26)
